text:
Morgan Frost has 12 points in 18 games for Calgary, which is about what you'd want from a 15-minute center. The breakdown is less comfortable. He has one goal in his last ten games, his own chances have thinned to 1.5 expected goals over that stretch, and his ice time is down a minute. Headlines are already asking what the Flames should do with him.

His scoring rate is running ahead of his talent range, mostly on assists (8 of them, 6 points on the power play). At five on five Calgary is slightly under water with him, 48% of the expected goals.

The case for patience is last season. Evolving-Hockey had him 73rd among 401 forwards in wins above replacement despite teammates in the bottom 7% by impact, and Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking had him carrying the puck in on 61% of his entries with most of his shots off the rush. Our projection is about 46 points. He needs linemates who can finish what he starts.
headline: Frost's assists are carrying a quiet start
